key_insight: Strain-space hyperreduction extends EMSL, ECM, and E3C to large-deformation solid mechanics, enabling much faster reduced models without sacrificing accuracy.
engineering_relevance: This gives engineers a practical way to simulate nonlinear solids with parameterized loads and materials far more efficiently than standard displacement-space ECSW.
method: Use boundary-consistent offline lifting to enforce arbitrary Dirichlet boundary conditions by construction.
Form hyperreduction directly in strain space with strain-space EMSL, ECM, and E3C.
Compare against standard displacement-space ECSW on hyperelastic test cases.
evidence_signal: On two hyperelastic examples with parameterized material behavior and deformation, the strain-space methods outperformed displacement-space ECSW, with E3C achieving about 10,000x speedup and EMSL about 100,000x while maintaining high accuracy.
watch_item: The approach still requires offline preprocessing and careful selection of the reduced strain basis and sampling strategy to balance setup cost, runtime, and accuracy.
paper_title: Efficient strain-space hyperreduction in large-deformation solid mechanics
